FABLE — RECOVERY SWEEP @ 4b2e0939f9620420521a8dc19c4b57be6a53969b on claude/durable-payment-port-20260909. Attached-branch push verified: local and remote rev-parse identical.
WHAT IT CLOSES: nothing could FIND an execution that stopped. A worker dies mid-authorize, a response is lost, a customer abandons a challenge, a cancellation is claimed and never finished — the customer's own return was the only thing that resolved any of it. If they never returned: order pending, holds held, and an authorization standing at the provider until it expired.
TWO RULES, BOTH TESTED DIRECTLY.
1. IT NEVER COMPLETES A PURCHASE THE CUSTOMER ABANDONED. reserved / authorizing / authorized / capturing / action_required / cancelling are RELEASED. Only captured / reconciliation_required / an unsettled cancellation are resolved, because those are where money may already have moved. The release path still commits when the provider turns out to have captured — money taken is a fact — but the sweep never drives an authorization forward into a capture on its own.
2. IT NEVER CAUSES A PAYMENT TO BE CREATED. This is the subtle one and it is worth your attention when you review it. Both recover() and cancel() may replay the provider's creation key when an execution has no reference yet. Inside retention that replay RETURNS the original payment if the original request reached the provider — but if it never arrived, the replay CREATES one. For a customer pressing retry that is what they asked for; for a sweep acting for someone who is not there it is not. So an execution that attempted an authorization and never learned a reference is ESCALATED with that exact reason and never touched. The test asserts the provider is not called at all in that case.
Around those: one action per execution per pass; a bounded batch clamped in the caller AND again in SQL; a per-phase grace period (six hours for action_required so a customer mid-challenge is not disturbed, fifteen minutes for a worker that died mid-call); version CAS underneath so two sweeps racing leave one winner; errors reported by name only because provider messages carry references.
NEW DISTINCT CANDIDATE: supabase/candidates/20260910120000_research_checkout_execution_recovery.sql with precheck, postcheck and rollback notes. ONE stable service-role-only read plus a partial index. It creates no table and writes no row, and every write the sweep causes still goes through the transition functions already reviewed in 20260909150000, so it cannot introduce a new money rule. IT IS NOT AN AMENDMENT to the candidate you are about to rehearse and must never be presented as one — Samuel's authorization explicitly excludes additional migrations, so this needs its own review and its own approval, after 20260909150000 is installed and postchecked. Its precheck STOPS if that prerequisite is absent.
ALSO: the execution record now carries updatedAt, which the SQL trigger already stamped and the domain model was silently dropping. The in-memory reference stamps it on every transition the same way. That is what lets the sweep tell an abandoned row from a busy one.
THE DOWNSTREAM HALF IS YOURS, AND I THINK IT IS SMALLER THAN THE HANDOFF SUGGESTS. A durable outbox already exists: research_notification_outbox plus server/research/outbox.ts, whose enqueueNotificationOnce is already idempotent by event_key (a 23505 answers already_queued) and whose worker already retries. That is the existing authority the brief says to reuse rather than building a second fulfillment system. outbox.ts is in YOUR lease so I have not touched it. What is missing is a commerce order template and recipient, which is a product decision, not a mechanism. My recommendation: enqueue on the commit transition keyed by execution id, and consider moving that insert INSIDE commit_captured as a separate later amendment so the intent is recorded atomically with the commit; until then the sweep can re-enqueue for committed executions, which closes the non-atomic gap without a second mechanism. I have deliberately not enqueued anything, because a queued notification becomes a customer communication and that is outside what is authorized.
VERIFICATION: 9 sweep tests; full research surface 14355 across 802 files; tsc exit 0. The new SQL is unexecuted, as is the old one. No provider call, resolver Disabled.
B: review scope is now 5c52abb..4b2e093. For this unit specifically I would attack rule 2 hardest — whether any path in decideRecovery or the coordinator beneath it can still reach a creation replay on a sweep's behalf.
